CustomDimensions.ExtractionsHelp: This is optional. A regex can be used to extract the value for this Custom Dimension from a page URL or page title automatically. This way, the custom dimension value does not have to be set manually via a Tracking client. A value still can be set manually via the Aspendora Tracker API. Dimension values set manually in tracking clients always takes precedence over extractions. If multiple extractions are defined, the first extraction that matches is used. You don’t need to escape forward slashes as Aspendora does this for you automatically. For example, use /news/ instead of \/news\/.

General.ComplianceCNILDescription:
This table shows how specific Aspendora configuration settings align with %1$sCNIL guidance%2$s on consent-exempt audience measurement. It is provided for informational purposes only and does not constitute legal advice or guarantee full compliance. To rely on CNIL's consent exemption, all required configurations must be correctly implemented.

  • If a setting is marked non-compliant, the exemption conditions are not satisfied and valid user consent must be obtained.
  • If a setting is marked unknown, Aspendora cannot determine whether the requirement has been met; these items must be verified manually by you, the publisher/controller.

To assess your overall compliance make sure you consult your legal advisors for a definitive compliance assessment.
Click %3$shere%4$s to access the Aspendora Self-Assessment, learn more about the CNIL criteria for consent-exempt analytics and understand how to configure Aspendora for CNIL exemption.

PrivacyManager.AnonymizeIpDescription: Select "Yes" if you want Aspendora not to track fully qualified IP-Addresses.
PrivacyManager.AnonymizeIpExtendedHelp: When users visit your website, Aspendora will not use the full IP address (such as %1$s) but instead Aspendora will anonymize it first (to %2$s). IP address anonymisation is one of the requirements set by the privacy laws in some countries such as Germany.
PrivacyManager.AnonymizeReferrerNote: Aspendora stores from which URL (referrer) a user comes to your site. In some cases such a URL may contain information that can be considered personal information. If you want to prevent such information to be tracked you can restrict the amount of referrer data that Aspendora will store when a visitor enters your website. The more information is removed from the referrer information, the less likely personal information will be recorded. The more information you remove from the referrer, the less clear it will be how a visitor came to your website.
PrivacyManager.AnonymizeUserIdHelp:
When you enable this option, the User ID will be replaced by a pseudonym to avoid directly storing and displaying personally identifiable information such as an email address. In technical terms: given your User ID, Aspendora will process the User ID pseudonym using a salted hash function.

Note: replacing with a pseudonym is not the same as anonymisation. In GDPR terms: the User ID pseudonym still counts as personal data. The original User ID could still be identified if certain additional information is available (which only Aspendora and your data processor has access to).

PrivacyManager.GdprChecklistDesc2: Find below our tools that let you exercise your users’ rights easily, and the list of actions to take to make your use of Aspendora compliant with the GDPR and safeguard your data. Visit our %1$sGDPR User guide%2$s to learn even more.
PrivacyManager.GdprOverviewApplicabilityIntro: If your Aspendora configuration processes personal data, GDPR will apply to your organisation, if it:
PrivacyManager.GdprOverviewIntro2: If you take steps to ensure no personal data is collected in Aspendora, then you may not be concerned by the GDPR for Aspendora (if you track no IP addresses, no user IDs, no geolocation data, etc.), but ePrivacy laws will still apply.
PrivacyManager.GdprOverviewMatomoPersonalData: If you are using Aspendora, you may be processing various personal data, depending on your configuration.
PrivacyManager.HandlingPreviouslyCollectedDataDetails: Anonymisation must be irreversible, meaning the data can no longer be linked to an individual. If anonymisation is not possible, deletion may be required. Anonymisation within Aspendora environment only can be managed through the Privacy Manager in Aspendora.
PrivacyManager.OptOutCodeTypeExplanation: The opt-out can either be set by using the Aspendora tracker code which means less code to add to your website pages and less likely to need updating in the future, or using standalone code which is more likely to work for visitors with script blockers but will need to be updated on each webpage if you change any settings.
PrivacyManager.OptOutExplanationIntro: This code will create a section where your visitors can opt-out of Aspendora tracking by setting an opt-out cookie in their web browser. See below (or %1$sclick here%2$s) to view the content that will be displayed.
PrivacyManager.OptOutUseTracker: Use the Aspendora tracker code to set the opt out
PrivacyManager.PluginDescription: Increase Privacy for your users and make your Aspendora instance privacy compliant with your local legislation.
PrivacyManager.PseudonymizeUserIdNote: When you enable this option, the User ID will be replaced by a pseudonym to avoid directly storing and displaying personally identifiable information such as an email address. In technical terms: given your User ID, Aspendora will process the User ID pseudonym using a salted hash function.
PrivacyManager.PseudonymizeUserIdNote2: Note: replacing with a pseudonym is not the same as anonymisation. In GDPR terms: the User ID pseudonym still counts as personal data. The original User ID could still be identified if certain additional information is available (which only Aspendora and your data processor has access to).
PrivacyManager.SecurityProceduresDesc1: Apply our %1$ssecurity recommendations%2$s in order to keep your Aspendora data safe.
PrivacyManager.SecurityProceduresDesc2: Check that you have a written contract with the company providing you the Aspendora server or hosting which ensures %1$sappropriate safeguards are provided%2$s.
PrivacyManager.SecurityProceduresDesc3: Include Aspendora in your %1$sdata breach procedure%2$s.
PrivacyManager.SecurityProceduresDesc4: Include Aspendora in your %1$sdata privacy impact assessment (DPIA)%2$s, if applicable.
PrivacyManager.TeaserHeader: On this page, you can customize Aspendora to make it privacy compliant with existing legislations, by: %1$s anonymizing the visitor IP%2$s, %3$s automatically remove old visitor logs from the database%4$s, and %5$s anonymize previously tracked raw users' data%6$s.
PrivacyManager.UnderstandingYourLegalObligationsBulletE: Exemptions for Privacy-Friendly Analytics: Some analytics solutions meeting strict conditions (e.g., anonymisation, aggregation, no cross-site tracking, opt-out provided, other requirements) can be used without consent, but with opt-out enabled (France, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands). Read more about the %1$sCNIL consent exemption for Aspendora%2$s.
PrivacyManager.UnderstandingYourLegalObligationsIntro1: Aspendora provides privacy-focused analytics that can be configured to align with any privacy law.
PrivacyManager.UnderstandingYourLegalObligationsIntro2: Before you configure Aspendora for your websites or apps, consult your legal or privacy advisers to determine which privacy laws apply to you.
PrivacyManager.UseSiteSpecificSettingsHelpText: By default, each site uses anonymization settings defined for the whole Aspendora instance in %1$ssystem settings%2$s. If you select the '%3$s' option, you can override each of the settings for this specific site.
